title: Ephemeral lease routing and hosted backfill constraints
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Context: We need a routing policy that allows tenants with Dedicated capacity to hold ephemeral "lease" slots for short bursts while enabling controlled hosted backfill when Dedicated capacity is exhausted. Goal is to minimize failed requests and keep SLOs while preventing noisy-tenant thrash on hosted.

Scope: design, implement, and rollout: 1) ephemeral lease token per tenant with TTL and renewal policy, 2) admission controller that prefers Dedicated slots but allows host spillover with rate caps, 3) variant demotion rules when model variant isn't available in Dedicated, 4) telemetry and circuit-breaker thresholds for automated backfill throttling.

Considerations:
- Lease TTL tradeoff: longer TTL reduces churn but hurts fairness. We propose default 30s TTL with tenant-configurable window up to 5m.
- Renewal vs reacquire: prefer lightweight renewal to avoid cold-starts.
- Cost control: hosted backfill should be rate-limited by per-tenant budget velocity and global emergency budget.
- Latency SLOs: hosted responses must be annotated to enable downstream feature-level fallbacks.

Artifacts:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.internal.redwood/episodes/ephemeral-lease-routing
- Proto/Config schema: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/leases-configs
- Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1987
- Dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/leases/ephemeral-backfill

Out-of-scope: policy UI and Console controls (handled in separate PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Dedicated-first behavior observed in canary region: >=99.5% requests routed to Dedicated when requested and capacity available
Hosted backfill capped: no tenant causes >5% sustained hosted-usage increase across region
Telemetry emits lease_acquired, lease_renewed, lease_expired, backfill_started, backfill_capped events
Rollout plan validated: canary region + smoke tests, progressive cross-region rollout with kill switch
